title: Canonical open restriction commutes with total tensor complexes
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary open, and P,N any unbounded complexes of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let R be over-site restriction followed by the canonical over equivalence to O_U-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], R(Tot(P tensor N)) is isomorphic as a complex to Tot(R(P) tensor R(N)). No K-flatness, quasi-coherence or boundedness is required.

source.place: Lemma 36.3.9, proof of (1), locality calculation; Tag 01CD for functorial tensor comparison

proof.text: The pure-tensor restriction formula gives a tensor comparison in each bidegree. Naturality follows by testing both module-map composites on pure tensors before sheafification; both send s tensor t to the tensor of the images. Transport this comparison from Scheme.Modules.restrict U.ι to the overFunctor/overEquiv composite using the canonical restriction identification.

Restriction preserves arbitrary coproducts. Apply its coproduct comparison to the sum over all p+q=n and the bidegree tensor comparisons to obtain inverse maps in each degree n. This uses the direct-sum total tensor, including its infinite sums for unbounded inputs.

Naturality intertwines the first and second differentials. Additivity intertwines multiplication by the integer sign (-1)^p on the second differential. The degreewise maps and inverses therefore commute with the total differential and yield the required complex isomorphism. For empty U or a zero input all terms are zero.
